title: Inhabitation and selection of margin-retaining exchange-stable Ds states
statement: On the DS15/DS16 class: (a) INHABITATION - do margin-compatible one-point exchange-stable sequences exist almost surely as N -> infinity, and does any such sequence satisfy DS14's full eventual hypotheses? Is v*(kappa) or v*+(kappa) attained by a margin-compatible population-stationary rule? A single finite state passing measured mass, conditioning, separation, and stability checks does not answer this sequence-level question. Measured: margin-retaining non-global stable states exist in every census instance at N <= 14, but the tested free-ascent terminals at N = 100..1000 lie in the funnel. (b) SELECTION - does exchange ascent from documented seeds converge in value to v_K almost surely, so DS16 forces terminal degeneracy? Finite runs support this but do not prove it. (c) DESIGN - construct a margin-constrained or penalized exchange method that reaches DS14-certified sequences with a stated gap to a correctly defined constrained value. DS16 proves a strict existential population price but neither constrained-value attainment nor one-sided continuity in kappa.
